solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink in club used by second team

indicators.note: the club is taken up by, so placed after, the second team

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
a driver is a golf club for long tee shots

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink at the clubhouse frequented by the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a social club, but it is the golf club; 'used by' puts the club after the second team.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Left outside, possibly in this

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone shut out of the group may find themselves alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges L (left) with the letters of OUTSIDE; the whole clue also describes the state of someone left outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left outside a group puts one in a state of being alone, which is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Mob constantly repeated phrase about very loud artist

parts.note: a riff is a short musical phrase repeated over and over
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A crowd chants a repetitive refrain about a noisy painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word meaning concerning; the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff are disreputable common people, a rabble or mob.

clue.text: Entry system at home

parts.note: a way of doing things is a system or method
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A door-entry system installed at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in is an entrance, a means of entry.

clue.text: Report outcome of tight ballot?

definitions.meaning: a close election result often triggers a second count of the votes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to tell a story and a further count of votes after a close result.

clue.text: Rogue out of house and home

parts.note: a villa is a large house
in means at home

explanation.surface: A scoundrel turned out of his house and home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is a link meaning 'made from', not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person, a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: River rose, unexpectedly forming a lake

indicators.note: unexpectedly tells us the letters fall into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A river's level rose suddenly and flooded into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges the nine letters of RIVER ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake used to store water.

clue.text: Vehicle in front

definitions.meaning: the ..., short for vanguard, is the foremost part

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a motor vehicle and the leading position, as in the vanguard.

clue.text: Girl turned up after six in capital

indicators.note: after places the turned name following the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman arrived in the capital after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads the name upwards, giving ENNA, and 'after' places it behind the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Count is more insensitive

definitions.meaning: numb means without feeling, so more numb is more insensitive

explanation.definitionFit: The word read one way is a quantity, read another a comparative of numb.

clue.text: Eminent newspaper grabbed by Myrna, US actress

indicators.note: grabbed by means the paper is held inside the actress's surname

parts.note: Myrna Loy was a Hollywood film star
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A distinguished paper snatched up by a Hollywood star.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is this very newspaper, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means high or exalted, as eminent people are.

clue.text: Poor souls come to find amphitheatre

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are badly made and must be reworked

explanation.surface: Unfortunate people gather at an ancient arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is the great amphitheatre of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Sailor, with a giddy aunt, carrying large spider

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold another letter inside them

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: giddy suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor with a dizzy aunt holding a huge spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giddy' rearranges just the aunt to ANTU; the sailor, the jumbled aunt and the a are 'carrying' L, which sits before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider.

clue.text: Line of fruit Oscar disregarded

indicators.note: disregarded means that letter is ignored and dropped

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grower's line of produce that one Oscar ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line of products, as in a product line.

clue.text: Shortage female in charge discovered in altered diet

indicators.note: discovered in means these letters are found inside the other piece
altered tells us the word is changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman running a kitchen finds supplies short in a changed diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges the diet into DEIT, and 'discovered in' finds the female and in-charge abbreviations inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount by which something falls short, a shortage.

clue.text: Charlie censored cracking climax

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: cracking suggests the word is broken apart and its pieces reset

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie censors a scene at its high point.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a build-up to a peak, so loosely a climax.

clue.text: Small number about at this time of day

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A modest count taken at a particular hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals the shortened form of number; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, a particular time of day.

clue.text: Rebuke agent and film producer Hal

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
Hal Roach produced Laurel and Hardy comedies

explanation.surface: Criticising a talent agent and a Hollywood producer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or scold them.

clue.text: Characters on pitch fitting a standard image

parts.note: type means printed characters, letters
to cast is to pitch or throw

explanation.surface: Players on a sports field matching a stock picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a playing field; it is the verb to throw. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor typecast is fitted repeatedly into the same stereotyped kind of role.

clue.text: A pool, nothing more

definitions.meaning: ... means no more than, as in 'a ... child'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a body of standing water and an adjective meaning only or simply.

clue.text: Back last nag, not first

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: not first means the opening letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a nag is a horse, usually a poor one

explanation.surface: A punter backs the final horse in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a betting verb, which suits the surface, and it is also the definition: to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or support a person or proposal.

clue.text: Black magic the Church of England's unhappy about

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: sorry means sad or unhappy
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The established church is upset about witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is witchcraft, the use of black magic.

clue.text: Shrub no good planted in Mediterranean country

indicators.note: planted in means the abbreviation is set inside the country's name

parts.note: Syria has a Mediterranean coast

explanation.surface: A worthless bush is planted in a Middle Eastern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the genus name for lilac, and also used for mock orange, both shrubs.

clue.text: Blue celestial body close to Mercury

parts.note: Earth is a planet, a celestial body

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A blue planet lies near Mercury in the solar system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' suggests a colour; here it means rude, risque. 'close to' looks like nearness in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is bawdy, and earthy also means crude or coarse.

clue.text: Dispense with popular composer

parts.note: to chop something is to cut or get rid of it
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Dropping a well-liked composer from the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin was a Polish Romantic composer of piano music.

clue.text: Notice wine's in short supply for this special purpose

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: in short supply means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: hock is a German white wine; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An announcement that the wine is running low.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', meaning arranged for one particular purpose.

clue.text: Evil drug, an unknown quantity

parts.note: dark can mean wicked or evil
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A wicked narcotic of unknown effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a competitor about whom little is known, an unknown quantity.

clue.text: Expected journalist to support dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means to stand underneath the other piece

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
ED, editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter anticipated being asked to back a dance event.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoped means wished or expected something to happen.

clue.text: Type of cricket pad turnin' askew

indicators.note: askew suggests things are out of line, so the letters are set crooked

explanation.surface: A cricketer's leg pad twisting out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'askew' rearranges PAD TURNIN. Tip-and-run is an informal game of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is a casual variety of the game where any touch of the bat obliges a run.

clue.text: Shopping centre in La Paz development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters are built into something new

explanation.surface: A new mall being built in the Bolivian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges LA PAZ; 'in' is a link. La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square, and in North America also a shopping centre.

clue.text: Urge to make money in Tokyo

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a strong craving and the Japanese currency unit.

clue.text: What shops do is obvious

definitions.meaning: stores unlock in the morning and close at night
a clear-cut case is plain and easily settled

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase describes a shop's daily routine; idiomatically it means clear-cut and obvious.
